text:
alex: heads up — after the load run i see a bunch of TIME_WAIT sockets and fd growth when using the Python AsyncClient in a worker loop. not closing sockets until process restart. anyone seen this?

nina: saw something similar yesterday during canary. repro with ~400 concurrent tasks hitting the same client instance.

ben: can you paste a tiny repro? curious if it's SDK or httpx underlying pool.

alex: sure — minimal example:
```py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def do(n, client):
    await client.generate("hello")

async def main():
    client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")
    for _ in range(100):
        await asyncio.gather(*(do(i, client) for i in range(200)))
    # no explicit aclose() here, client used across batches

asyncio.run(main())
```

sam: that pattern (long-lived client + repeated gather) used to be fine. looks like after a failed request the underlying pool isn't drained.

nina: repro notes: SDK 0.13.2, python 3.11, uvloop. if i add `await client.aclose()` between batches the socket leak goes away. so finalizers aren't firing.

dev-bot: created issue redwood/devex#1827 (async-conn-leak) :bug:

ben: ok two likely culprits: 1) __aexit__/aclose not awaiting outstanding request tasks, 2) retry/backoff interaction holding semaphores and preventing drain. i've seen semaphore counts not decrement when task is cancelled mid-retry.

alex: exactly — i saw semaphore count stuck at high value in the debug logs after a 429 flood. new requests get queued forever.

qa-automation: reproduced with this config: CONCURRENCY=256, RETRIES=3, BACKOFF=exp. Observed: sockets not closed + pending tasks accumulating.

nina: workaround for now: create a fresh AsyncClient per batch and always await aclose() in finally. not great for perf but unblocks testing.

ben: i'll draft a PR to: (a) ensure __aexit__ and aclose explicitly cancel & await any inflight requests, (b) add finally blocks that call transport.aclose(), (c) add integration test that fires 500 concurrent tasks and asserts no fd leak.

sam: also request we add a health endpoint on client that exposes internal semaphore counts for debugging (`client.metrics().conn_semaphore`). useful for debugging production regressions.

alex: minor typing/UX nit: AsyncClient.__aexit__ signature currently typed as -> None which confuses mypy; should be -> Optional[bool] to match context manager protocol. can we include that in the change?

ben: yes will add typing fix + changelog note.

nina: one more thing — retry middleware swallows CancelledError and doesn't release the retry semaphore in some code paths. will add unit tests that simulate cancellation during backoff.

dev-bot: linked PR #1894 from ben: fix(async): ensure async client drains pool & fix semaphore edgecases

qa-automation: test plan for PR: load job that runs for ~10 minutes with periodic 429 bursts, assert no fd growth and eventual success rate > 99% after retries.

alex: thanks everyone — any perf regression risk from eagerly cancelling tasks in aclose()? we should measure.

ben: agreed — add a non-blocking graceful window (500ms) before force-cancel, configurable via client arg `graceful_shutdown_ms`. will include perf benchmark in PR.

nina: :thumbsup: lgtm. once PR lands let's cut a patch and push to canary.

sam: tagging infra: @ops — load runner will retest once patch is live.

alex: nice. saved my weekend. :relieved:
